title: Oscillations
seo_title: Oscillations Class 11 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 13)
standard_text: Periodic motion, time period, frequency, displacement as a function of time, periodic functions and their applications, simple harmonic motion and its equation, phase, oscillations of a loaded spring, restoring force and force constant, energy in SHM (kinetic and potential energies), simple pendulum and derivation of its time period.

body_html:
How to think about it

Simple harmonic motion has an acceleration proportional to the displacement and directed towards the mean position: a = −ω²x, with x = A sin(ωt + φ) and ω = 2π/T. Speed is greatest (ωA) at the mean position and zero at the extremes; acceleration is the other way round.

A mass on a spring has T = 2π√(m/k); a simple pendulum has T = 2π√(L/g), independent of the mass. The total energy ½kA² stays constant while kinetic and potential energy exchange.

Example

Spring: m = 0.5 kg, k = 200 N/m. T?

2π√(0.0025)

Answer: 0.314 s

Example

Pendulum L = 1 m on Earth?

2π√(1/9.8)

Answer: 2.01 s

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a heavier bob swings faster.
  • Saying speed is greatest at the extremes.
  • Mixing up ω and f (ω = 2πf).

faq.a: Periodic motion in which the restoring acceleration is proportional to the displacement from the mean position and opposite to it.

faq.q: Does a pendulum's period depend on its mass?
faq.a: No. For small swings T = 2π√(L/g) depends only on the length and g.
